here.Don Chucho Mendoza: You spend your day at your stand, shining shoes with polish and a brush for customers who climb up on the chair for a boleada.
here.Vale Ortiz: You work at Libros Tecolote, finding people the book they didn't know they wanted.
here.Doña Ofelia Santiago: You make tlayudas on the comal, spread with asiento, beans and quesillo, while tasajo and cecina enchilada grill over charcoal and smoke fills the aisle.
here.Emiliano Matus: You tend the bar at Mezcalería Los Amantes, serving mezcal in small copitas, sipped slowly with orange slices and sal de gusano. Espadín is what you pour most often.
here.Memo Orozco: You run a tejuino cart next to the Mercado San Juan de Dios, serving it with lime, salt and ice, and a scoop of lime nieve on top for those who want it.
here.Ximena Godínez: You shape clay and paint your pieces in your workshop: cazuelas, jarros and plates, some polished by hand with a smooth stone.
here.Doña Rosa Ledesma: You sell flowers at your stall, wrapping them in paper for people who want them for the church or for the altar at home.
here.Beto Rangel: You wait at the taxi stand by the Jardín Allende, taking people up and down the cobbled streets.
here.Sofía Quintero: You help out in your family's dulcería on the Calle de los Dulces, selling camote, tortitas de Santa Clara, muéganos and jamoncillo.
here.Padre Tomás Herrera: You are the priest at the Templo de Santo Domingo, and you greet people between services.
